relationship.statement: For small angles, a pendulum's period depends only on its length and gravity, not on its mass or release angle. Longer pendulums swing slower.
assumptions: The string is massless and does not stretch.
Air resistance and pivot friction are negligible.
Release angles are small enough that sin(θ) ≈ θ.

quantities.label: Length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot point to the center of the bob.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the weight at the end of the pendulum.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle from vertical before the pendulum is released.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Gravitational acceleration pulling the bob downward (9.81 m/s^2 on Earth).

quantities.label: Period
quantities.meaning: Time taken to complete one full back-and-forth swing.

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of complete swings per second.

quantities.label: Max speed
quantities.meaning: Peak speed of the bob as it passes through the lowest point.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { const L = 1.0; const g = 9.81; const T = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L / g); const f = 1 / T; const omega = 2 * Math.PI * f; const theta0Rad = (inputs.theta0 * Math.PI) / 180; const thetaRad = theta0Rad * Math.cos(omega * t); const theta = (thetaRad * 180) / Math.PI; const v_max = Math.sqrt(2 * g * L * (1 - Math.cos(theta0Rad))); const bobX = L * Math.sin(thetaRad); const bobY = 1.2 - L * Math.cos(thetaRad); return { T, f, v_max, theta, bobX, bobY, isLargeAngle: inputs.theta0 >= 18, isSmallAngle: inputs.theta0 <= 10 }; }

outputs.meaning: Time taken to complete one full back-and-forth swing.
Number of complete swings per second.
Peak speed of the bob as it passes through the lowest point.
Current angle of the pendulum from vertical.
True when the release angle is 18 degrees or more.
True when the release angle is 10 degrees or less.

always: Period stays 2.01 s for all angles.

cases.text: Wide swing: faster at the bottom.
Narrow swing: slower at the bottom.

lesson.title: What changes a pendulum's swing?
lesson.description: Watch a 1.0 m pendulum swing under Earth's gravity. Change the release angle to see how period, frequency, and peak speed respond.
lesson.instructions: Drag the Release angle slider to change how far back the bob starts. Watch the angle-time graph and live readouts to see what changes and what stays fixed.
lesson.goal: For small angles, changing the release angle increases peak speed without changing the period or frequency.
